lead_headline: Blossom by SYC preps Highland opening as July restaurant tracker heats up — 5 new leads land overnight

restaurant.blurb: 5 new leads today: Blossom by SYC (Chinese, LoHi), Funny Plus closure (Korean, Aurora), plus three expansions tracking. Active pipeline now 292 (159 openings, 133 closures).

liquor.blurb: 88 new applications today — the deluge continues. Highlights: Hammer and Nails (men's grooming/beer-wine, Capitol Hill and DTC), Clairvoyance (tavern/cabaret, Santa Fe Arts), Celeste (tavern, South Broadway), Seedstock Brewery (brewpub, West Colfax), Barcelona Wine Bar (Belleview), Doubles Club (entertainment license, RiNo pickleball concept), SYC Omakase (Cherry Creek), The Henry (Fillmore). Plus Trader Joe's #307 filing for fermented malt at Louisiana, Chestnut Cellars liquor store on Chestnut Place. Status shifts: Tacos El Metate and #Vybe cleared delinquency to active, Honey Elixir Lounge flipped delinquent. Week explodes to 424 applications vs. zero prior week — state licensing pipeline fully operational post-freeze. Today's haul spans every category from grooming shops to airport kiosks (six DIA vendors active). The 45-day blackout is officially over.

reputation.blurb: 3 citations yesterday — Wednesday ticks slightly above Tuesday's 2-mention floor but remains well below pre-weekend averages. Week limps to 69 mentions across 17 sources, now tracking 13% below last week's 79 as the three-week uptrend definitively snaps. Instagram still leads at 16, Denver Post 13, Facebook 13, Reddit 8, Hoodline 4. Notable Wednesday pickups: Denverite covering tax-funded immersive theater eviction downtown, San Antonio Express-News running Canyon Lake resort condo conversion (Missouri developer angle), Reddit post on Denver's mixed-use rezoning push. The slowdown accelerates: daily acquisition now averaging 2.3 mentions vs. 11.3/day needed to match prior week's pace. Source diversity flat at 17 outlets. Five days remain in the tracking window — barring a Friday surge, this week marks the first sequential decline after three weeks of growth.

subscriptions.blurb: Net +1 yesterday (1 new, 0 canceled) — the first positive session in thirteen days breaks the churn spiral. MTD improves slightly to −15 (−1.0/day), 90-day cumulative at +93. But the recovery is fragile: past 7 days still show −24 net (17 new, 41 canceled) vs. prior week's +1 — a devastating 25-subscriber swing that confirms July as the worst acquisition month on record. Since July 1, just 18 new subscribers against 41 cancellations for a −23 monthly net. Yesterday's single addition doesn't reverse the trend: cancellation rate still running 2.3:1 against sign-ups across the fortnight. The thirteen-day losing streak (July 3–15) erased 38 net subscribers before Wednesday's micro-bounce. YTD net holds at +211 (+1.1/day) only because Q1-Q2 momentum carried forward. If July's −23 pace persists through month-end, it will mark the first negative monthly close in tracking history.
